title: Tag Document Bootstrap Delivery
summary: generate and link one Analysis tag document for every current canonical tag, rebuild the complete collection, and stop for management review
content_html:
Tag Document Bootstrap Delivery

Target Result

One guarded migration creates a new public document in the Analysis tags sub-scope for every current canonical tag without a doc_id, copies the registry description into that document once, and stores the allocated ID in the registry row.

The current planning snapshot contains 245 flat registry tags with no doc_id and three independent sub-scope documents. If that snapshot remains the cutover input, the delivery creates 245 new linked sources and leaves the three existing sources unchanged, producing 248 manageable documents in total. Execution must freeze and report the actual counts again.

This is a bootstrap, not feature closeout. It makes the complete real collection available so its navigation, discovery, metadata, and source-editing needs can be reviewed before follow-on work is chosen.

Frozen Output Contract

For each input registry row, the migration allocates one immutable document ID and creates:

---
doc_id: <allocated immutable document ID>
title: "<tag_id>"
added_date: <cutover timestamp>
last_updated: <cutover date>
parent_id: ""
viewable: true
---
# <tag_id>

**<group>**

<tag registry description>

The corresponding registry row gains that exact doc_id. The migration preserves tag order, tag_id, scalar group, description, row timestamps, policy, aliases, assignments, and the three existing tag documents.

The registry schema advances only far enough to retain and validate an optional unique doc_id during the feature transition. The bootstrap populates it for every frozen input row; making it required for later New Tag and Edit Tag writes belongs to follow-on delivery work.

In Scope

  • Add one repository-owned preview/write/validate command for this one-off bootstrap.
  • Require the current flat registry schema, unique tag IDs, one allowed scalar group per tag, a description string, and no pre-existing registry doc_id values.
  • Inventory every existing Analysis tags source before allocating IDs.
  • Produce an inspectable preview containing the exact tag-to-document mapping, target paths, source count, registry projection, and input fingerprints.
  • Allocate immutable IDs without matching documents by title, group, or content.
  • Create every new Markdown source with exclusive-create semantics before atomically replacing the registry.
  • Add and validate unique registry doc_id values while preserving every pre-existing tag value and all alias and assignment sources.
  • Rebuild the Analysis documents, sub-scope manifest, and by-ID payloads; reload the local management inventory; and confirm the sub-scope documents remain excluded from parent-scope search.
  • Reconcile the complete registry-to-document relationship and inspect the resulting collection through the delivered sub-scope management workflow.

Not In Scope

  • Reusing, rewriting, moving, linking, or deleting the three existing tag documents.
  • Changing New Tag to create a document.
  • Adding doc_id to Edit Tag or implementing stale-link repair.
  • Synchronizing registry descriptions with document content in either direction.
  • Changing tag deletion or document deletion behavior.
  • Adding group data, filtering, styling, or management fields to the public sub-scope manifest.
  • Redesigning the report, metadata editor, source editor, or management toolbar.
  • Creating Tag semantic-token targets.
  • Editing the generated prose beyond the fixed one-time seed template.

Any discovery, filtering, bulk action, repair, or authoring need revealed by the real collection becomes separate follow-on work.

Delivery Steps

Current state: accepted and closed. The reviewed plan was applied exactly, the Analysis outputs were rebuilt and reconciled, and the complete collection was accepted through the management review gate. Narrow-layout review and any resulting management changes remain separate follow-on work.

  1. [x] Freeze the input. Record the registry version and hash, exact tag count and order, zero current registry doc_id values, allowed groups, alias and assignment hashes, and the exact existing Analysis tags source inventory.
  2. [x] Build the guarded preview. Project the complete immutable ID map, Markdown sources, registry rows, target paths, and reconciliation counts without writing. A preview is invalidated by any registry or source-inventory change.
  3. [x] Review the exact cutover. Confirm every tag appears once, every allocated ID and path is unique, every source matches the fixed template, the three existing sources are untouched, and only doc_id plus the registry-level schema metadata change in canonical tag data.
  4. [x] Apply once. Create only the previewed new source paths, replace the registry atomically after all source writes succeed, and report any run-created unreferenced files precisely if the registry commit cannot complete.
  5. [x] Rebuild and reconcile. Build the Analysis document payloads, reload the management inventory, and confirm parent-scope search still excludes sub-scope documents. Prove every registry doc_id is unique and resolves to its exact generated source and public detail URL. Prove aliases, assignments, descriptions, and the three pre-existing documents are unchanged.
  6. [x] Review management and stop. Use the local managed tags report to inspect the complete inventory and representative generated and pre-existing detail, metadata, source, and Back/Forward behavior. Record concrete friction, the unexercised narrow-layout case, and follow-on candidates without implementing them in this delivery.

Applied Evidence

  • Reviewed plan: var/studio/tag-document-bootstrap/review-plan.json
  • Frozen input: tag_registry_v3, 245 ordered tags, zero doc_id fields, three existing tag sources, 70 aliases with 71 targets, and eight assignment references.
  • Frozen registry, alias, assignment, and existing-document inventory fingerprints: 184cb1654608f02214bacb0d6d727cb35bb3136ad1ce41589dae97f67f8c26ed, 9bdcd5ac7df75719ba791480ff45612137ce1832e5c0595eaf8e23a376701158, 08c0dba8bf923be376f1b8186290a00b1a2bdb7c74ad811f896eb1f430b72d5d, and c3257e5936ad99651725ff86166df0490838c71c2f2e273924b63a998321f2dd.
  • Applied output: 245 new unique sources, 248 final documents, tag_registry_v4, no target-path collision, and group counts of 72 subject, 35 domain, 67 form, and 71 theme.
  • The applied registry preserves every ordered tag row and row timestamp, adding only its planned doc_id; only the top-level registry version and timestamp also change. All 245 source hashes match the fixed template.
  • Mapping fingerprint: 5e5f4ade4e493998e7499f5a78c2a6aa5e43a3d537afdb99d599fd232e7311e7. Applied registry fingerprint: e7d5bf765e7e1183b02ec47eec6c6fa8ae0aacd2ab28d25685328ba4571e2564.
  • Source, public-manifest, and by-ID payload inventories each contain 248 documents. All 245 linked registry IDs resolve through all three surfaces and derive the expected managed detail URL. The three pre-existing sources, aliases, and assignments are byte-identical to the frozen inputs.
  • The parent Analysis search output contains no tag subdocuments. The Analysis build completes with zero warnings, and the management inventory reports 248 viewable documents.
  • Focused bootstrap and adjacent tag-model tests pass 34/34. The maintained studio-tag-smoke profile passes 11/11; its summary is var/admin/test-runs/tag-document-bootstrap/summary.md. Explicit Python compilation and lint pass for the planner, command, validation seam, tests, and maintained check registration. git diff --check passes.

Management Review

The initial managed desktop review at a 1280 by 720 viewport confirmed that the 248-row report loads, generated and pre-existing details render, metadata and parent/subdocument source controls are available, detail-to-list Back/Forward history works, and the browser console remains clear.

The complete flat alphabetical list is long. Independent pre-existing and generated documents can also share a visible title, so entries such as bird and nerve are not distinguishable in the list. These are review findings, not changes in this delivery. Narrow-layout behavior was not exercised because the controlled browser exposed no viewport-resize capability; this omission was accepted at closeout and remains available for a separate follow-on review.

Likely Authority

  • studio/data/canonical/tags/tag-registry.json
  • a focused studio/commands/ bootstrap command
  • a focused studio/services/tags/ projection and validation module
  • studio/services/tags/tag_source_model.py
  • studio/services/tags/tag_write_transactions.py
  • docs-viewer/services/docs_document_identity.py
  • docs-viewer/scopes/analysis/source/sub-scopes/tags/documents/
  • docs-viewer/build/build_docs.py
  • docs-viewer/build/docs_builder/sub_scope.py
  • docs-viewer/build/build_search.py
  • focused bootstrap projection, command, and reconciliation tests

These are inspection starting points. The command owns the one-off cross-application composition; ordinary Tag Registry and Docs Viewer UI paths do not become migration hosts.

Completion And Evidence

  • The reviewed preview and applied output report the same registry fingerprint, tag order, tag-to-document mapping, target paths, and counts.
  • Exactly one new immutable document exists for every frozen input tag, and every frozen input registry row contains its unique exact doc_id.
  • Every linked ID resolves in the Analysis tags sub-scope and derives a workable /docs/?scope=analysis&doc=d-20260624-213316-478639&subdoc=<doc_id> URL.
  • The three pre-existing sources are byte-identical, remain independent, and are included alongside the generated documents in the management inventory.
  • Registry descriptions remain present and unchanged after seeding. Aliases and assignments are byte-identical.
  • Focused projection/command tests, the Analysis document build, explicit parent-search exclusion checks, canonical JSON validation, git diff --check, and exact source/payload counts support only the bootstrap claims above.
  • Manual review records how the complete collection behaves and ends at a decision gate for separate follow-on delivery documents.

Durable Destinations

After the bootstrap is accepted, record the transitional registry field and one-time generation result in Tag Registry and Tag Source Data.

Any accepted management change belongs to Manage Sub-Scope Documents or a new focused successor, not to this bootstrap delivery.
